# Rafiq v0.4.26 — Copilot sign-in that sticks

Signing in to GitHub Copilot could fail again and again with «403 Forbidden», or get stuck on «GitHub hasn't received your approval». This release fixes both.

---

## 🔑 What was going on

When Copilot refused a fresh sign-in for a moment, Rafiq threw away the GitHub sign-in that had worked and asked for a new one. GitHub lets an app create only a limited number of sign-ins per hour. So every retry made the next one more likely to fail, until GitHub started asking for an extra confirmation in the browser and the approval never reached Rafiq.

## ✅ What changed

- **The sign-in is kept.** If GitHub accepts the sign-in, Rafiq saves your account even if Copilot refuses at that moment. Trying again later needs no new sign-in.
- **Copilot's 403 explains itself.** It now opens the Copilot guide, which covers turning Copilot on, account policies, VPN, and waiting a few minutes after several sign-ins in a row.
- **The waiting message says where to look.** If the approval doesn't come through, check the GitHub page in your browser: after several sign-ins within an hour, GitHub asks you to confirm again.

> **If you hit this before updating:** wait about an hour, then sign in once.

---

**Updating:** installed copies offer this update on their own. New installs: download `Rafiq_0.4.26_x64-setup.exe` below and check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\Rafiq_0.4.26_x64-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
```
